item.title: Backup and Restore
item.description:
Description

Backup exports a graph’s schema, vertices, and edges as JSON data. Restore imports that data into a target graph. These HugeGraph-Tools commands support migration, recovery after an upgrade, and graph merging.

Backup

Backup runs in any graph mode. Pausing source writes before exporting is recommended to keep schema, vertices, and edges consistent (paginated read APIs do not provide a global transactional snapshot). Note: backup -t all only exports schema and graph data, excluding deployment configurations and user permissions.

item.title: HugeGraph Docker Cluster Guide
item.description:
Overview

Docker Compose provides a quick way to run a complete HugeGraph distributed cluster (PD + Store + Server) on Linux or macOS.

Prerequisites

  • Docker Engine 20.10+ or Docker Desktop 4.x+
  • Docker Compose v2
  • For a three-node cluster on macOS, allocate at least 12 GB of memory (Settings → Resources → Memory). Adjust resources to suit other platforms.

Tested environments: Linux (native Docker) and macOS (Docker Desktop on ARM M4).

item.title: FAQ
item.description:
Deployment and startup

Choose RocksDB or HStore

For development, testing, or small-to-medium standalone deployments, Server + RocksDB is recommended for its simplicity and high performance. When data volume is large (TB to PB scale) or requires horizontal scalability and multi-replica high availability, deploy an HStore distributed cluster (PD + Store + Server).

Version 1.7.0 supports RocksDB, HStore, HBase, and Memory. Legacy backends such as Cassandra, ScyllaDB, MySQL, and PostgreSQL require a version earlier than 1.7.0. See the Server quick start for deployment steps.

item.title: Security Report
item.description:
Reporting New Security Problems with Apache HugeGraph

Warning

Production security requirements

HugeGraph disables user authentication by default. In production, enable authentication and authorization, set white_ip.status=enable, maintain the IP allowlist, and grant minimum permissions. Do not expose Gremlin, Cypher, or other query endpoints directly to the public network. See the IP allowlist API. Isolate the Server process, for example with Docker or Kubernetes.

Standard Server configuration writes authentication-proxy audit records to audit-*.log. Retain these files and restrict read access. auth.audit_log_rate controls the maximum per-user log output rate rather than serving as a dedicated audit-log on/off switch.

item.title: 1.8.0 shared-foundation migration
item.description:
The 1.8.0 shared-foundation migration changes Java imports and extension signatures, and requires Server, PD and Store to upgrade together. Use this guide to identify affected code, rebuild your integrations and check existing data before deployment.

Find the work that applies to you

Your integration What to prepare
Java code using Server IDs, schema metadata, queries or indexes Update imports and affected signatures, then recompile against matching 1.8.0 artifacts.
Custom serializers, HugeGraph implementations or element subclasses Adapt the SPI contracts and shared element state below.
Custom Gremlin imports or scripts Replace the old IdGenerator class name and test packaged Gremlin startup.
Hubble, Java client or Computer integration Apply the downstream exception changes when matching artifacts are available.
HStore deployment Align the PD namespace, inspect legacy rebuilt indexes and upgrade all writers together.
Loader or another REST-only caller Keep the independent client DTOs; migrate any actual affected Java calls.

This shared-foundation consolidation targets HugeGraph 1.8.0. Use matching Server, PD, Store and downstream artifacts when upgrading. See the source migration guide for Java mappings and compatibility fixtures.

item.title: HugeGraph 1.8.0 Gremlin Migration & Compatibility Guide
item.description:
HugeGraph 1.8.0 upgrades its underlying graph traversal and query framework from Apache TinkerPop 3.5.1 to TinkerPop 3.8.1, requires Java 17 for Server and builds, and updates the script engine to Groovy 4.0.25.

This upgrade introduces several language-level breaking changes. The sections below cover the most frequently affected syntax and behavioral changes first; less common edge cases and lower-level protocol details are in the Full Compatibility Reference at the end.

Note
  • This guide applies to upgrades from version 1.7.0 (or earlier) to 1.8.0.
  • The Groovy script engine remains supported in 1.8.0; existing multi-line scripts, variable definitions, and Java closures continue to work in most cases.

Top 5 High-Frequency Syntax and Behavioral Changes

The following 5 changes affect the most queries. Changes 1–3 cause immediate execution errors if not rewritten; changes 4–5 do not raise errors but silently alter returned results (dropping elements with missing properties or passing unmatched branches through). Review these first.
